input: A new-to-market pet grooming product ('Combat Comb') from a startup brand entering an unfamiliar product category, with the goal of producing shelf-ready packaging suitable for distribution in major retailers. No prior packaging existed for this product; the agency (Catalpha) started from the physical product itself.

workflow_steps.step_name: Measuring Up (Determine Package Size, Type & Structure)
workflow_steps.step_description: The agency took careful physical measurements of the product (width, length, depth) and used them to determine the package type and structure, selecting a hanging box with a display window so the packaging would optimize shelf space while still showing the product's function.
workflow_steps.input: Physical 'Combat Comb' product; target retail shelf environment
workflow_steps.action: Measure product dimensions (width/length/depth); select structural package type (hanging box with window) based on shelf-space and product-visibility needs
workflow_steps.output: Product measurements; chosen structural concept (hanging box with window)
workflow_steps.professional_rule: Shelf-ready retail packaging structure must be chosen to optimize shelf space while still visually communicating the product's function, not decided on aesthetics alone.

workflow_steps.step_description: Using the measurements from step_01, the agency trimmed a rough blank physical prototype to further test the design and internal structure, using it to work out sizing, stock (paper) weight, and the folding required for internal structural elements such as the angled platform and window placement.
workflow_steps.input: Product measurements and notes from step_01
workflow_steps.action: Build a rough blank physical mockup; test sizing, stock weight, and required folding of internal structural elements
workflow_steps.output: Validated physical mockup with confirmed sizing, stock weight, and folding parameters
workflow_steps.professional_rule: Physical prototyping (blank mockups) is required to validate stock weight and folding feasibility before any digital dieline work begins.

workflow_steps.step_name: Initial Creative Exploration (Design Visuals for Client Review)
workflow_steps.step_description: The agency developed four distinct design concepts, each varying visual look, copy, and messaging, evaluated against three explicit goals: (1) jump off the shelf, (2) clearly communicate what the product does and how it benefits the shopper, (3) create a solid branded look. These were presented to the client for feedback.
workflow_steps.input: Validated structural mockup from step_02; brand/product positioning goals
workflow_steps.action: Generate four design concept layouts with copy/messaging variations; present to client against the three stated goals
workflow_steps.output: Four design concept layouts presented for client review and feedback
workflow_steps.professional_rule: Concept design is evaluated against explicit, named criteria (shelf impact, clear product communication, brand consistency) rather than aesthetic judgment alone.

workflow_steps.step_name: Dieline Drafting (Create Digital Dieline for Print Production)
workflow_steps.step_description: With design concepts out for client feedback, the agency drafted the actual production dieline needed to lay out the package for final printing, sized from the mockup measurements and modified to account for internal structural elements. The dieline's accuracy was checked periodically using 3D software.
workflow_steps.input: Client feedback on design concepts (step_03); validated mockup measurements (step_02)
workflow_steps.action: Draft a digital dieline accounting for proper folding, paper (stock) weight, and print feasibility; periodically verify dieline accuracy using 3D software
workflow_steps.professional_rule: A dieline must be engineered to account simultaneously for folding, stock weight, and print feasibility, and its accuracy must be checked with 3D software rather than trusted as a flat 2D layout alone.

workflow_steps.step_name: Final Package Production (Lay Out Full Package on Dieline for Print)
workflow_steps.step_description: After the client chose one design layout (with edits) to move forward with, the agency laid out the full approved package artwork — including product photography, feature callouts, and graphics emphasizing the product's function — onto the verified dieline. 3D software was used again throughout as a check, since flat layouts can look correct but require adjustment in 3D.
workflow_steps.input: Client-approved design layout with edits (step_03/step_04 outputs); verified dieline (step_04)
workflow_steps.action: Lay out final approved artwork (photography, feature callouts, graphics) onto the dieline; re-check via 3D software
workflow_steps.professional_rule: Flat 2D layouts must be re-verified in 3D before finalization because visual correctness in 2D does not guarantee correctness once folded.

workflow_steps.step_description: The final package design was printed and the product was launched into major retailers.
workflow_steps.action: Print packaging; distribute product into major retail channels
workflow_steps.output: Physical, launched packaging on shelf in major retailers

final_outputs: Print-ready digital dieline and final package artwork
Physical shelf-ready package (hanging box with window) launched in major retailers
Product/feature photography and graphics used on the final package
professional_constraints: Retail shelf-space optimization drives structural package type choice (hanging box with window)
Physical product must remain visible/legible through packaging to communicate function
Structural integrity constraints: sizing, stock (paper) weight, and folding must be validated via physical mockup before digital work
Dieline must simultaneously satisfy folding requirements, stock weight, and print feasibility
3D software verification is used at two separate points (dieline drafting and final production) because flat 2D layouts can misrepresent the folded 3D result
Design concepts are judged against explicit stated goals: shelf impact, clear product communication, brand consistency
Client feedback/approval gates exist between creative exploration and dieline drafting, and again before final production layout
production_or_delivery_requirements: A physical blank mockup/prototype is required before any digital dieline is drafted
Digital dieline must be print-production ready (accounts for paper weight, folding, print feasibility)
Final artwork must be laid out directly onto the verified dieline, not designed independently of it
Client sign-off on a chosen layout (with edits) is required before final production layout begins
